title: The $\ell$-adic diagonal class over the completed coefficient sheaf
statement:
With the notation of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system]:

1. $R\varprojlim_n\Delta_*\mathbf Z/\ell^n=\Delta_*\Zl$ and
   $R\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/\ell^n(1)=\Zl(1)$, and more generally derived
   direct image along any morphism of the pro-étale sites considered commutes
   with $R\varprojlim$ and is computed levelwise on inverse systems.
2. The Tate twist $(1)$, defined as tensor product over the completed
   coefficient sheaf with the invertible sheaf $\Zl(1)$ (and $(-1)$ with its
   dual), is exact, preserves products and commutes with $R\varprojlim$.
3. $R\varprojlim c_\bullet$ is a morphism
   $\delta_{\Zl}:\Delta_*\Zl\to\Zl(1)[2]$ of derived $\ell$-complete objects; it
   is the derived $\ell$-completion of $\partial$, and it is in a unique way a
   morphism in $D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},\Zl)$ over the completed coefficient sheaf
   $\Zl$ of $W$. Its reductions modulo $\ell^n$ are the torsion cycle classes.

proof.text: For the reduction towers $(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_n$ and $(\mu_{\ell^n})_n$, the transition maps are epimorphisms: the first are quotient maps and the second are the power maps identified in [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system](3), which are surjective by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](1), applicable because $\ell$ is invertible on $W$. The statement of [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic] says that an epimorphic tower has $R\varprojlim$ equal to its ordinary limit, so these limits are respectively the completed coefficient sheaf $\Zl$ and $\Zl(1)$ by the inverse-limit definition of the twist and the completed coefficient identification in [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. The diagonal is a closed Cartier divisor: on an affine chart with local equation $t$ as in [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system](1), its open complement is $D(t)$. Distinguished affine opens are quasi-compact, so the complementary open immersion is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] over $\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+1}$ to each quotient transition (regarding its target as a module over that same ring): the direct-image tower again has epimorphic transitions. Therefore [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic] also identifies its derived limit with its ordinary limit. The latter is $\Delta_*\Zl$, since direct image is precomposition on sections and sheaf inverse limits are computed sectionwise. For an arbitrary morphism $g$ of the schemes considered, the induced morphism of pro-étale topoi, with the canonical identification of the inverse image of the constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ (or the canonical map on completed coefficient sheaves), is a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. The inverse systems here are towers of $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$-modules, not of modules over the completed coefficient sheaf, so we use the tower comparison stated for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi: [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] gives the evaluation identifications $\operatorname{ev}_nRg_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet\cong Rg_*M_n$ and the canonical isomorphism $Rg_*R\lim M_\bullet\simeq R\lim(Rg_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet)$, with the total derived limit whose Roos triangle is that of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]; this is the asserted commutation and levelwise computation.

The definition [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] makes $K(1)$ the derived tensor product with the locally free rank-one sheaf $\Zl(1)$ and defines $(-1)$ using its dual. More specifically, [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](2) proves that the inverse limit $\Zl(1)$ is locally free of rank one over the completed coefficient sheaf, with the stated finite reductions. Apply the tensor clause of [det-formal-closed-support-ii-limits] with $X=Z=S=W$, both $i$ and $u$ the identity, and open complement empty, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z_\ell$. Tensoring with this rank-one sheaf is exact because after the stated trivializing cover it is the identity on module sheaves; the cited tensor clause says it preserves products and fibers, and the natural map from tensoring $R\varprojlim$ to the $R\varprojlim$ of the tensors is an isomorphism. On a pro-etale trivializing cover, the dual of $\Zl(1)$ is identified with the dual of the free rank-one completed coefficient module, hence is again free of rank one; these local identifications descend to the dual sheaf. Apply the same tensor clause of [det-formal-closed-support-ii-limits] to this dual finite-locally-free module: its tensor functor preserves products and fibers and the natural map from tensoring $R\varprojlim$ to the $R\varprojlim$ of the tensors is an isomorphism. This gives exactness, product preservation, and $R\varprojlim$-commutation for $(-1)$ and proves clause (2).

Apply $R\varprojlim$ to $c_\bullet$. By [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system](2), $R\varprojlim\circ T$ is derived $\ell$-completion, while [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system](3) identifies the source and target systems; step (1) therefore identifies the resulting morphism with $\Delta_*\Zl\to\Zl(1)[2]$ and shows that both objects are derived $\ell$-complete. The map is initially linear over the constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$. Specializing clause (1) of [sk-lem-integral-models] to $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ identifies restriction of scalars from the completed coefficient sheaf with an equivalence on derived complete objects, so there is a unique $\Zl$-linear morphism $\delta_{\Zl}$. For the final reduction use [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction] with the constant ring $\Lambda=\mathbf Z_\ell$, $I=(\ell)$, and $K$ equal to either $\Delta_*\mathbf Z\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbf Z}\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ or $\mathbf G_m[1]\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbf Z}\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$. Tensor associativity identifies their strict reduction towers with the two towers of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system]; each finite quotient is perfect, represented over $\mathbf Z_\ell$ by the two-term free resolution for multiplication by $\ell^n$. The cited reduction theorem identifies the finite reduction of the derived limit with its level-$n$ term; hence the reduction of $\delta_{\Zl}$ is $c_n$, which is the torsion diagonal class by clause (4) of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system]. To identify these reductions with reductions over the completed coefficient sheaf, apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] to $A=\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $I=(\ell)$ on $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Its canonical comparisons identify constant-coefficient finite reduction with completed-coefficient finite reduction, commute with the quotient transitions, and carry the completion unit to the constant-coefficient unit. Thus completeness of the displayed completed-coefficient endpoints follows from their constant-coefficient completeness, and the reduction calculation just made is the one in $D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},\Zl)$ required by clause (3).
